extraFacts.fact: EN 837-1 classifies Bourdon-tube pressure gauges by accuracy class, the maximum permissible error as a percentage of the full scale span; the standard classes are 0.1, 0.25, 0.6, 1, 1.6, 2.5 and 4, so a gauge stated at 1.6% FSD is class 1.6 and one at 1% FSD is class 1.
extraFacts.source: EN 837-1:1996 (Bourdon tube pressure gauges: dimensions, metrology, requirements and testing)

extraFacts.fact: Gauge scale ranges are normally chosen so the working pressure sits in the middle third of the dial; a glycerine fill damps pointer flutter from pump pulsation and vibration; a dry gauge has no fill.

faqs.q: What is the Dynamic Fluid Components CDS 1.5" dry gauge, 1/8" NPT used for?
faqs.a: The Dynamic Fluid Components CDS 1.5" dry gauge, 1/8" NPT is a dry Bourdon-tube pressure gauge with a 1.5" dial and 1/8" NPT connection, accurate to 1.6% FSD. It reads in psi, bar and is listed in 30 ranges on the [pressure gauges shelf](/c/ic-pressure-gauges).

faqs.q: What do the letters at the end of CDS gauge part numbers such as CDS-4V-000A mean?
faqs.a: The last letter is a manufacturer option code: several part numbers share one range and differ only in that code. For the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT, CDS-4V-000A and CDS-4V-000D are two such codes, so quote the full part number or tell us how the gauge mounts and we confirm the option.

faqs.q: Which pressure ranges does the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT come in?
faqs.a: The DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT comes in 14 ranges, from 30” Hg – 0 psi to 0–4000 psi, including a compound vacuum-and-pressure scale. All 30 part numbers use the 1/8" NPT connection; the size table lists every range.

faqs.q: How do I pick the range of the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT?
faqs.a: Pick a scale whose full reading is roughly twice the normal working pressure, so the pointer sits mid-dial and pressure spikes stay on the scale. For example a line that runs at 300 psi suits a 0–600 psi scale where the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT is offered; see the [how to choose a pressure gauge range](/blog/how-to-choose-a-pressure-gauge-range).

faqs.q: How accurate is the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT?
faqs.a: The DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT is accurate to 1.6% FSD, meaning the error is within 1.6% of full scale. EN 837-1 would call that accuracy class 1.6; a lower figure is a tighter gauge, and the 4" CFC and PDSS series carry 1% FSD against 1.6% on the 1.5", 2" and 2.5" gauges.

faqs.q: What is the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT made of?
faqs.a: The DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT has a Steel case, a polycarbonate lens, a phosphor bronze Bourdon tube and a bronze connection. It has no liquid fill, so the pointer is more affected by vibration; see [glycerine-filled vs dry pressure gauges](/blog/glycerine-filled-vs-dry-pressure-gauges).

faqs.q: Which standard is the accuracy of the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT stated to?
faqs.a: The listing for the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT states 1.6% FSD and names no gauge standard. EN 837-1 gives accuracy classes by percentage of span, so this corresponds to class 1.6. If you need a calibration certificate, ask on your [request](/contact) before ordering.

faqs.q: What thread does the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT screw into?
faqs.a: The DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT has a 1/8" NPT connection in bronze. Match the thread to the port, and see the [instrumentation tube fittings](/c/instrumentation-tube-fittings) for adapters and fittings that connect a gauge to a line.

faqs.q: How do I mount and protect the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT?
faqs.a: Screw it in by its 1/8" NPT connection, sealing the thread, and keep the 1.5" dial where it can be read. Where the line pulsates, fit a snubber or needle valve to protect the Bourdon tube; the pressure gauge guide covers safe mounting.

faqs.q: Where is the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT typically used?
faqs.a: A 1.5" dry gauge with a 1/8" NPT connection suits hydraulic and pneumatic equipment, pumps and power units where a local pressure reading is needed. For oilfield frac and cementing lines see the oilfield instrumentation range.

faqs.q: How does the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT differ from the DFC CDS 2" gauge?
faqs.a: The [DFC CDS 2" gauge with 1/4" NPT](/p/dynamic-fluid-components-cds-2-in-compound-dry-pressure-gauges-1-4-in-npt) has a 2" dial against 1.5" and a 1/4" NPT connection against 1/8" NPT; the DFC CDS 1.5" gauge with 1/8" NPT has 30 part numbers against 64.
